text.p: Indonesia telecommunications provider PT Indonesian Satellite Corp (Indosat) said on Tuesday it had won a contract to build an earth station for a unit of the London-based International Maritime Satellite (Inmarsat).
Indosat's public relations manager J.B. Basuki said the firm had won the tender from ICO Global Communication Services to build the Satellite Access Note station, expected to be operational by 2000.
Construction, costing some $10 million, is expected to begin next year in Banyuurip, Gresik in East Java, he said.
Basuki said Indosat won the contract to build the earth station to cover the Pacific and Indian oceans in a tender in which several Asian companies participated.
Inmarsat is a global consortium comprising 78 companies, including Indosat which joined in 1987.
The consortium operates its own telecommunication satellites and provides data, voice and other services.
